The construction is given exactly: 'a vertex labelled U gets the projection Π_U onto U along U^⊥, except sources: -Π_{U_a} at X_a, else 0=Π_0'. It is a definition, so there is nothing further to derive.
'The negative source makes every route's endpoint difference Id ... Π_{U_a^⊥}+Π_{U_a} from X_a to Y_a, Π_F-0 elsewhere', using F=U_a⊥U_a^⊥ from nondegeneracy.
's_b=(W_bm-2N+2L_b)+N=W_bm-(N-2L_b)', from the absolute-change budget plus one extra rank per X_a source.
The number appears only in the citation '=W_bm-N+2L_b =177176569088785861287000000<W_bm'. It is correct: I recomputed it from W_b, N and L_b.

'a vector of U' minus its projection onto U lies in U'∩U^⊥, so F=U⊥(U'∩U^⊥)⊥U'^⊥ ... Π_{U'}-Π_U projects onto U'∩U^⊥ and has rank dim U'-dim U, as does its negative on a reversed edge'. This is the paper's argument, spelled out.

'So each edge's rank is its absolute dimension change, except the first edge of each X_a'. This follows because every other vertex matrix is the projection onto its label (0=Π_0 at the other sources).
'at stage 1, B=0, so it joins U_a to [F|<t_{a_1}>]=U_a with zero change, yet its matrix Π_{U_a}-(-Π_{U_a})=2Π_{U_a} has image the line U_a and rank one'.
'The deficit W_bm-s_b=N-2L_b=339/539 N is positive as L_b/N<1/2', with L_b/N=100/539 derived earlier.
'Π_{U_a^⊥}+Π_{U_a} from X_a to Y_a, Π_F-0 elsewhere'. These are the X_a case and the zero-source, identity-sink case of the other roles, as in the paper.
